title: HA2F: Dual-module Collaboration-Guided Hierarchical Adaptive Aggregation Framework for Remote Sensing Change Detection
abstract: Remote sensing change detection (RSCD) aims to identify the spatio-temporal changes of land cover, providing critical support for multi-disciplinary applications (e.g., environmental monitoring, disaster assessment, and climate change studies). Existing methods focus either on extracting features from localized patches, or pursue processing entire images holistically, which leads to the cross temporal feature matching deviation and exhibiting sensitivity to radiometric and geometric noise. Following the above issues, we propose a dual-module collaboration guided hierarchical adaptive aggregation framework, namely HA2F, which consists of dynamic hierarchical feature calibration module (DHFCM) and noise-adaptive feature refinement module (NAFRM). The former dynamically fuses adjacent-level features through perceptual feature selection, suppressing irrelevant discrepancies to address multi-temporal feature alignment deviations. The NAFRM utilizes the dual feature selection mechanism to highlight the change sensitive regions and generate spatial masks, suppressing the interference of irrelevant regions or shadows. Extensive experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed HA2F, which achieves state-of-the-art performance on LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and SYSU-CD datasets, surpassing existing comparative methods in terms of both precision metrics and computational efficiency. In addition, ablation experiments show that DHFCM and NAFRM are effective. \href{https://huggingface.co/InPeerReview/RemoteSensingChangeDetection-RSCD.HA2F}{HA2F Official Code is Available Here!}

title: Developing an Automated Practice Environment and Feedback Engine for Guided Instruction in the Deformable Bodies Course
abstract: Mathematical problem solving is a fundamental competency demanded by employers and an integral component of engineering education. We seek to improve instruction in mathematical concept-based engineering courses. To this end, we created an interactive problem solving environment that provides targeted feedback on a student's problem solving attempts by having them work mathematical exercises in a dedicated intuitive software interface. We provide syntactic feedback that is independent of the problem statement, as well as semantic feedback. Semantic feedback is achieved by systematically comparing the ground-truth solution for the exercises provided by the instructor with the student's attempt and reconstructing appropriate error messages based on the differences detected between the solutions. Our systematic approach is based on analyzing the dependencies between equations used by the student, and comparing either individual equations or a reduced representation of a sequence of equations with each other to identify and report differences. We conducted a study to evaluate the quality of the feedback provided by the system. We also conducted surveys on usability of the interface. Based on the studies conducted, we prove the effectiveness of the system and the engine both as a tool for providing rapid and accurate assessment of correctness of exercise attempts.

title: ИДЕНТИФИКАЦИЯ И ВЕРИФИКАЦИЯ МНОГОФАКТОРНЫХ ПРЕДИКТОРОВ СЛОЖНОСТИ ТЕКСТА В АСПЕКТЕ ПРЕПОДАВАНИЯ РУССКОГО ЯЗЫКА КАК ИНОСТРАННОГО
abstract: В статье представлено корпусное исследование, направленное на выявление и верификацию объективных лексико-синтаксических предикторов сложности учебных текстов для изучающих русский язык как иностранный (РКИ). На материале текстов, стратифицированных по уровням CEFR (A1–C2), с помощью статистической среды R был проведён анализ четырёх ключевых параметров: лексического разнообразия (характеристика K Юла), синтаксической сложности (средняя длина предложения и средняя дистанция синтаксической зависимости) и стилистических особенностей (соотношение существительных и глаголов). Результаты статистического анализа (критерий Краскела-Уоллиса и корреляция Спирмена) показали, что синтаксические предикторы и лексическое разнообразие являются высокозначимыми индикаторами, демонстрирующими сильную корреляцию с уровнем владения языком. Соотношение существительных и глаголов также выявило значимую тенденцию к номинализации в текстах более высоких уровней. Исследование предлагает многомерную модель для объективной оценки текстовой сложности и закладывает эмпирическую основу для будущих психолингвистических экспериментов.

title: IMMORTAL™ Framework: A Formal Mathematical Architecture for Organizational Persistence, Governance Resilience, and Long-Term Systemic Survivability
abstract: IMMORTAL™ Framework A Formal Mathematical Architecture for Organizational Persistence, Governance Resilience, and Long-Term Systemic Survivability Version 1.0 — Zenodo Scholarly Record Author / Rights Holder: Bidyut MazumdarORCID: 0009-0007-5615-3558DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18343196All Versions DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18343195Publication Date: 23 January 2026Resource Type: DatasetPublisher: Zenodo 1. Framework Overview IMMORTAL™ is a formal mathematical and computational architecture for studying organizational persistence, governance resilience, structural continuity, and long-horizon systemic survivability. The framework represents organizational persistence through a structured mathematical model in which multiple organizational or institutional subsystems are represented by bounded structural variables. These variables are combined through an aggregate persistence function, allowing the framework to express threshold conditions, sensitivity relationships, formal invariants, and system-level persistence requirements in a mathematically explicit form. The architecture is designed to connect: mathematical modeling; formal methods; symbolic computation; machine-checkable specification; governance-system analysis; organizational resilience; cybersecurity and systemic risk; temporal persistence reasoning; formal verification workflows; and long-horizon institutional continuity. IMMORTAL™ is therefore structured as a formal research architecture, rather than as a claim that any real-world organization is literally incapable of failure or dissolution. 2. Mathematical Foundation Let twelve structural matrices or subsystem measures be represented by [ M_i \in (0,1], \qquad i=1,\ldots,12. ] The aggregate structural persistence function is defined as [ \mathcal{I}(M)=\prod_{i=1}^{12}M_i. ] Within the framework's defined model, an organization is classified as structurally persistent when [ \mathcal{I}(M)\geq0.97. ] This threshold is a model-defined mathematical criterion and should not be interpreted as an empirical probability of organizational survival, a prediction of business longevity, or a guarantee of real-world institutional continuity. 2.1 Sufficient Component-Level Condition The framework specifies the sufficient condition [ \forall i,\quad M_i\geq0.9975. ] Under this condition, [ \mathcal{I}(M) \geq (0.9975)^{12} \approx 0.9704090818, ] and therefore [ \mathcal{I}(M)\geq0.97. ] Accordingly, the component-level threshold of 0.9975 for each of the twelve modeled dimensions is mathematically sufficient for satisfying the framework's aggregate threshold of 0.97. This relationship follows directly from the multiplicative structure of the model and is independently reproducible through ordinary numerical or symbolic computation. 3. Formal-System Architecture IMMORTAL™ organizes the persistence problem into a formal system consisting of: Definitions — precise descriptions of modeled entities, variables, predicates, and states. Structural Parameters — bounded representations of organizational subsystems. Aggregate Invariants — mathematical relationships connecting subsystem conditions to system-level persistence. Threshold Conditions — explicit criteria for classification within the model. Symbolic Encodings — machine-readable mathematical representations. Formal Proof Structures — theorem-oriented representations intended for proof-assistant verification. Temporal Logic Components — representations for persistence and state-transition reasoning. Governance Predicates — formal representations of selected governance and compliance properties. Executable Components — computational representations aligned with the specified mathematical structures. Verification Artifacts — documentation and formalization materials supporting reproducibility and inspection. The architecture is intended to maintain a traceable relationship between definition → specification → mathematical expression → formalization → computation → verification. 4. Formal Verification Architecture The corpus includes formalization and verification-oriented materials associated with Lean4, together with documentation addressing Coq and Isabelle/HOL and multi-prover verification. The purpose of this architecture is to make mathematical propositions and system invariants suitable for machine-assisted inspection rather than relying exclusively on informal mathematical exposition. The verification-oriented corpus addresses: theorem formulation; mathematical invariants; symbolic encodings; formal predicates; proof-assistant representations; executable specifications; cross-prover comparison; temporal logic; governance constraints; and verification-oriented documentation. A proof-assistant artifact can establish the correctness of a formally specified proposition within the assumptions and formal environment encoded in that artifact. Such verification should not be interpreted as empirical validation of every underlying real-world assumption, organizational measurement, governance outcome, or deployment context. 5. Symbolic and Computational Layer The symbolic layer provides a computational representation of the twelve structural dimensions and their aggregate relationship. The principal mathematical relationship is: [ \mathcal{I}(M)=\prod_{i=1}^{12}M_i. ] This formulation supports: deterministic numerical evaluation; symbolic manipulation; threshold analysis; sensitivity analysis; boundary-condition examination; formal theorem development; automated consistency checking; and reproducibility across compatible computational environments. The computational representation is intended to preserve correspondence between the mathematical specification and its executable implementation. 6. Temporal Persistence Logic Long-term organizational persistence is not solely a static mathematical property. Real systems evolve through sequences of states. Accordingly, the IMMORTAL™ corpus incorporates temporal reasoning and documentation concerning Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) and Computation Tree Logic (CTL). The temporal layer is intended to support formal analysis of questions such as: whether specified conditions persist across successive states; whether critical invariants eventually fail; whether specified recovery states remain reachable; whether governance constraints continue to hold over time; whether particular failure conditions can be reached; whether recovery or stabilization conditions remain possible; and how persistence properties interact with state transitions. Temporal-logic formalization concerns the behavior of a specified model. It does not, by itself, establish that an actual organization will behave according to that model. 7. Governance and Compliance Formalization IMMORTAL™ incorporates governance and compliance concepts into a formal modeling environment. Within the framework, properties such as: transparency; accountability; auditability; procedural integrity; institutional resilience; continuity; compliance; and structural responsibility may be represented as formal predicates, constraints, or system-state properties where sufficiently precise definitions are available. This approach seeks to move selected governance concepts from purely narrative descriptions toward explicitly defined, inspectable, and potentially machine-checkable conditions. Compliance within the mathematical model refers to compliance with the formal specification being evaluated. It does not constitute legal certification, regulatory approval, governmental authorization, or a determination that a real-world organization complies with any particular law or regulation. 8. Twelve-Dimensional Structural Model The twelve structural matrices constitute the central dimensional architecture of IMMORTAL™. Each matrix is intended to represent a distinct structural component of organizational persistence. The multiplicative formulation means that weaknesses in individual dimensions can materially affect the aggregate persistence value. This structure provides a formal basis for examining: dependency among organizational capabilities; cumulative structural weakness; threshold sensitivity; resilience requirements; systemic bottlenecks; continuity conditions; and minimum component-level requirements. The mathematical architecture therefore treats persistence as a system property emerging from the combined condition of multiple structural dimensions, rather than as a single-variable characteristic. 9. Formal Theorems and Proof Structure The release includes a dedicated Formal Theorems and Proofs artifact together with formal framework and verification documents. The theorem layer is intended to document mathematical propositions derived from the framework's definitions and assumptions. A formal theorem should be understood according to its precise statement and assumptions. In particular: mathematical validity depends on the stated premises; proof-assistant verification concerns the encoded formal proposition; formal verification does not independently validate empirical premises; model correctness does not establish real-world predictive accuracy; and mathematical sufficiency within the model does not constitute a guarantee of practical organizational survival. This distinction is fundamental to responsible interpretation of formal mathematical systems. 10. Machine-Readable and Proof-Oriented Formalization The corpus includes IMMORTAL.lean.pdf and associated formal verification materials. evidence.title: IMMORTAL™ Framework: A Formal Mathematical Architecture for Organizational Persistence, Governance Resilience, and Long-Term Systemic Survivability
evidence.abstract: IMMORTAL™ Framework A Formal Mathematical Architecture for Organizational Persistence, Governance Resilience, and Long-Term Systemic Survivability Version 1.0 — Zenodo Scholarly Record Author / Rights Holder: Bidyut MazumdarORCID: 0009-0007-5615-3558DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18343196All Versions DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18343195Publication Date: 23 January 2026Resource Type: DatasetPublisher: Zenodo 1. Framework Overview IMMORTAL™ is a formal mathematical and computational architecture for studying organizational persistence, governance resilience, structural continuity, and long-horizon systemic survivability. The framework represents organizational persistence through a structured mathematical model in which multiple organizational or institutional subsystems are represented by bounded structural variables. These variables are combined through an aggregate persistence function, allowing the framework to express threshold conditions, sensitivity relationships, formal invariants, and system-level persistence requirements in a mathematically explicit form. The architecture is designed to connect: mathematical modeling; formal methods; symbolic computation; machine-checkable specification; governance-system analysis; organizational resilience; cybersecurity and systemic risk; temporal persistence reasoning; formal verification workflows; and long-horizon institutional continuity. IMMORTAL™ is therefore structured as a formal research architecture, rather than as a claim that any real-world organization is literally incapable of failure or dissolution. 2. Mathematical Foundation Let twelve structural matrices or subsystem measures be represented by [ M_i \in (0,1], \qquad i=1,\ldots,12. ] The aggregate structural persistence function is defined as [ \mathcal{I}(M)=\prod_{i=1}^{12}M_i. ] Within the framework's defined model, an organization is classified as structurally persistent when [ \mathcal{I}(M)\geq0.97. ] This threshold is a model-defined mathematical criterion and should not be interpreted as an empirical probability of organizational survival, a prediction of business longevity, or a guarantee of real-world institutional continuity. 2.1 Sufficient Component-Level Condition The framework specifies the sufficient condition [ \forall i,\quad M_i\geq0.9975. ] Under this condition, [ \mathcal{I}(M) \geq (0.9975)^{12} \approx 0.9704090818, ] and therefore [ \mathcal{I}(M)\geq0.97. ] Accordingly, the component-level threshold of 0.9975 for each of the twelve modeled dimensions is mathematically sufficient for satisfying the framework's aggregate threshold of 0.97. This relationship follows directly from the multiplicative structure of the model and is independently reproducible through ordinary numerical or symbolic computation. 3. Formal-System Architecture IMMORTAL™ organizes the persistence problem into a formal system consisting of: Definitions — precise descriptions of modeled entities, variables, predicates, and states. Structural Parameters — bounded representations of organizational subsystems. Aggregate Invariants — mathematical relationships connecting subsystem conditions to system-level persistence. Threshold Conditions — explicit criteria for classification within the model. Symbolic Encodings — machine-readable mathematical representations. Formal Proof Structures — theorem-oriented representations intended for proof-assistant verification. Temporal Logic Components — representations for persistence and state-transition reasoning. Governance Predicates — formal representations of selected governance and compliance properties. Executable Components — computational representations aligned with the specified mathematical structures. Verification Artifacts — documentation and formalization materials supporting reproducibility and inspection. The architecture is intended to maintain a traceable relationship between definition → specification → mathematical expression → formalization → computation → verification. 4. Formal Verification Architecture The corpus includes formalization and verification-oriented materials associated with Lean4, together with documentation addressing Coq and Isabelle/HOL and multi-prover verification. The purpose of this architecture is to make mathematical propositions and system invariants suitable for machine-assisted inspection rather than relying exclusively on informal mathematical exposition. The verification-oriented corpus addresses: theorem formulation; mathematical invariants; symbolic encodings; formal predicates; proof-assistant representations; executable specifications; cross-prover comparison; temporal logic; governance constraints; and verification-oriented documentation. A proof-assistant artifact can establish the correctness of a formally specified proposition within the assumptions and formal environment encoded in that artifact. Such verification should not be interpreted as empirical validation of every underlying real-world assumption, organizational measurement, governance outcome, or deployment context. 5. Symbolic and Computational Layer The symbolic layer provides a computational representation of the twelve structural dimensions and their aggregate relationship. The principal mathematical relationship is: [ \mathcal{I}(M)=\prod_{i=1}^{12}M_i. ] This formulation supports: deterministic numerical evaluation; symbolic manipulation; threshold analysis; sensitivity analysis; boundary-condition examination; formal theorem development; automated consistency checking; and reproducibility across compatible computational environments. The computational representation is intended to preserve correspondence between the mathematical specification and its executable implementation. 6. Temporal Persistence Logic Long-term organizational persistence is not solely a static mathematical property. Real systems evolve through sequences of states. Accordingly, the IMMORTAL™ corpus incorporates temporal reasoning and documentation concerning Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) and Computation Tree Logic (CTL). The temporal layer is intended to support formal analysis of questions such as: whether specified conditions persist across successive states; whether critical invariants eventually fail; whether specified recovery states remain reachable; whether governance constraints continue to hold over time; whether particular failure conditions can be reached; whether recovery or stabilization conditions remain possible; and how persistence properties interact with state transitions. Temporal-logic formalization concerns the behavior of a specified model. It does not, by itself, establish that an actual organization will behave according to that model. 7. Governance and Compliance Formalization IMMORTAL™ incorporates governance and compliance concepts into a formal modeling environment. Within the framework, properties such as: transparency; accountability; auditability; procedural integrity; institutional resilience; continuity; compliance; and structural responsibility may be represented as formal predicates, constraints, or system-state properties where sufficiently precise definitions are available. This approach seeks to move selected governance concepts from purely narrative descriptions toward explicitly defined, inspectable, and potentially machine-checkable conditions. Compliance within the mathematical model refers to compliance with the formal specification being evaluated. It does not constitute legal certification, regulatory approval, governmental authorization, or a determination that a real-world organization complies with any particular law or regulation. 8. Twelve-Dimensional Structural Model The twelve structural matrices constitute the central dimensional architecture of IMMORTAL™. Each matrix is intended to represent a distinct structural component of organizational persistence. The multiplicative formulation means that weaknesses in individual dimensions can materially affect the aggregate persistence value. This structure provides a formal basis for examining: dependency among organizational capabilities; cumulative structural weakness; threshold sensitivity; resilience requirements; systemic bottlenecks; continuity conditions; and minimum component-level requirements. The mathematical architecture therefore treats persistence as a system property emerging from the combined condition of multiple structural dimensions, rather than as a single-variable characteristic. 9. Formal Theorems and Proof Structure The release includes a dedicated Formal Theorems and Proofs artifact together with formal framework and verification documents. The theorem layer is intended to document mathematical propositions derived from the framework's definitions and assumptions. A formal theorem should be understood according to its precise statement and assumptions. In particular: mathematical validity depends on the stated premises; proof-assistant verification concerns the encoded formal proposition; formal verification does not independently validate empirical premises; model correctness does not establish real-world predictive accuracy; and mathematical sufficiency within the model does not constitute a guarantee of practical organizational survival. This distinction is fundamental to responsible interpretation of formal mathematical systems. 10. title: Experimental data to assess speech rate comprehension, acceptability, and preference in Catalan Easy Language
abstract: English: This dataset contains the replication information for an experiment on speech rate comprehension, acceptability, and preference in Easy Language audio materials. It includes the transcripts of the audio stimuli and comprehension questions used in the study, the images associated with each audio, and the collected data from participants, including comprehension scores, age, Raven scores, preference and Likert scale assessments, and the correction strategies employed by participants during the second listening of the audios. The data was collected from three groups: (1) neurotypical Catalan native speakers, (2) neurotypical Catalan learners (A1/A2 level), and (3) Catalan native speakers with intellectual disabilities. Català: Aquest conjunt de dades conté la informació necessària per a replicar un experiment sobre velocitat de la parla en continguts d’àudio en lectura fàcil. L’experiment analitza la comprensió, l’acceptabilitat i les preferències dels usuaris. El conjunt de dades inclou la transcripció dels estímuls i les preguntes de comprensió que s’han emprat en l’experiment, les imatges associades a cada estímul, i les dades recopilades, incloent-hi els resultats de comprensió, l’edat dels participants, els resultats del test de Raven, les preferències i les valoracions amb les escales de Likert, i les estratègies de correcció que han fet servir els participants durant la segona audició dels àudios. S’han recollit les dades amb tres grups de participants: (1) catalanoparlants neurotípics, (2) estudiants de català (nivells A1/A2) neurotípics, (3) i catalanoparlants amb discapacitat intel·lectual. Español: Este conjunto de datos contiene la información necesaria para replicar un experimento sobre velocidad del habla en contenidos de audio en lectura fácil. El experimento analiza la comprensión, la aceptabilidad y las preferencias de los usuarios. El conjunto de datos incluye la transcripción de los estímulos y las preguntas de comprensión que se han empleado en el experimento, las imágenes asociadas a cada estímulo, y los datos recopilados, incluyendo los resultados de comprensión, la edad de los participantes, los resultados del test de Raven, las preferencias y las valoraciones con las escalas de Likert, y las estrategias de corrección usadas por los participantes durante la segunda audición de los audios. Se han recogido los datos con tres grupos de participantes: (1) catalanohablantes neurotípicos, (2) estudiantes de catalán (niveles A1/A2) neurotípicos, (3) y catalanohablantes con discapacidad intelectual.

title: O-MSDNet: An OCR-Enhanced Fine-Grained Multimodal Sarcasm Detection Approach
abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) is a technology that comprehensively uses text, image, voice and other multimodal information to recognize and understand human emotions more accurately. Multimodal irony detection is a challenging subdivision task in MSA. Existing methods mainly focus on the interaction between text and visual image, but ignore an important information source, namely scene text. Therefore, this paper proposes a fine-grained multimodal irony detection method based on OCR enhancement. As an auxiliary mode, it can capture deeper semantic conflicts. A large number of experimental results on the SarcNet dataset show that this method is significantly superior to the baseline model in accuracy and F1 score. The results further verify the effectiveness of O-MSDNet model for multimodal irony detection.

title: Photovoltaic Power Forecasting and Mechanism Analysis Based on Interpretable Deep Learning
abstract: Accurate short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is crucial for reliable power system operation under high renewable energy penetration. However, PV generation exhibits strong intermittency, nonlinear dynamics, and long-range temporal dependencies, which challenge conventional forecasting approaches. To address these issues, this paper proposes an Informer-based framework for short-term PV power forecasting that enables efficient modeling of long temporal sequences with reduced computational complexity. The proposed model employs probabilistic sparse self-attention to capture global temporal dependencies while maintaining scalability. Extensive experiments are conducted on real-world multi-station PV datasets, and the proposed approach is compared with statistical models, classical machine learning methods, and deep learning baselines. The results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves consistently superior performance across all stations, with an average RMSE of 3.47 MW, MAE of 1.98 MW, and$\mathbf{R}^{2}$of 0.95. Furthermore, SHAP-based interpretability analysis is incorporated to quantify feature contributions and reveal nonlinear and thresholddependent effects, enhancing the transparency of the forecasting process. The proposed framework provides an accurate, efficient, and interpretable solution for short-term photovoltaic power forecasting.

title: One-shot federated unsupervised domain adaptation with Smoothed Knowledge Distillation and teacher refinement
abstract: Federated unsupervised domain adaptation (FUDA) addresses the challenge of adapting models to an unlabeled target domain using decentralized source domains while preserving data privacy. However, existing FUDA methods typically require multiple communication rounds, rely on complex aggregation strategies, and often struggle with noisy pseudo labels and inconsistent source knowledge. To address these challenges, we propose SKD-ETR, a novel one-shot FUDA framework that combines Smoothed Knowledge Distillation (SKD) and Exponential moving average-based Teacher Refinement (ETR). SKD trains a student model on the target domain using smoothed soft pseudo labels generated by the ensemble of source models. This reduces overconfidence, mitigates noise, and improves robustness. ETR further refines each source model by interpolating its parameters toward the student via exponential moving average (EMA), thereby transferring target-domain knowledge back to the teachers. This bidirectional refinement enhances pseudo-label quality and student generalization without additional communication overhead. SKD-ETR eliminates complex aggregation by initializing the student model randomly and performing a single-round distillation process. Extensive experiments on OfficeHome, Office-Caltech, and DomainNet demonstrate that SKD-ETR achieves competitive performance while being communication- and computation-efficient, and robust under noisy supervision. The code for this paper is available at https://github.com/A-Abedi/SKD_ETR . • A one-shot FUDA framework using knowledge distillation without source data access. • Smoothed pseudo labels reduce noise and improve student model robustness. • Teacher refinement via EMA enhances generalization with no extra communication. • Random target model initialization avoids biased aggregation and enables efficient adaptation.

title: Predicting Startup Success Using Large Language Models: A Novel In-Context Learning Approach
abstract: Venture capital (VC) investments in early-stage startups that end up being successful can yield high returns. However, predicting early-stage startup success remains challenging due to data scarcity (e.g., many VC firms have information about only a few dozen of early-stage startups and whether they were successful). This limits the effectiveness of traditional machine learning methods that rely on large labeled datasets for model training. To address this challenge, we propose an in-context learning framework for startup success prediction using large language models (LLMs) that requires no model training and leverages only a small set of labeled startups as demonstration examples. Specifically, we propose a novel k-nearest-neighbor-based in-context learning framework, called kNN-ICL, which selects the most relevant past startups as examples based on similarity. Using real-world profiles from Crunchbase, we find that the kNN-ICL approach achieves higher prediction accuracy than supervised machine learning baselines and vanilla in-context learning. Further, we study how performance varies with the number of in-context examples and find that a high balanced accuracy can be achieved with as few as 50 examples. Together, we demonstrate that in-context learning can serve as a decision-making tool for VC firms operating in data-scarce environments.

title: Sistem Pakar Diagnosa Penyakit Kulit menggunakan Metode Certainty Factor dan Forward Chaining
abstract: This study focuses on developing an expert system for diagnosing skin diseases using the Certainty Factor and Forward Chaining methods. The increasing prevalence of skin diseases and the similarity in symptoms among different conditions make accurate initial diagnoses challenging without expert help. Expert systems are valuable in supporting early medical decisions and improving public access to diagnostic information. The study aims to diagnose skin diseases based on symptoms while considering the uncertainty in medical decision-making. The novelty of the study lies in integrating the Certainty Factor method to quantify confidence in diagnoses with the Forward Chaining inference mechanism, which processes symptom-based rules. A rule-based expert system approach is used, with data on symptoms and diseases gathered from literature and expert knowledge. Forward Chaining serves as the inference engine, while the Certainty Factor method calculates the certainty level of diagnoses based on user-selected symptoms. The results show that the expert system can accurately diagnose skin diseases and provide a certainty value aligned with expert opinions. The combination of Certainty Factor and Forward Chaining enhances the clarity and reliability of the diagnosis. The study concludes that the proposed system effectively supports the initial diagnosis of skin diseases by providing diagnostic results along with a certainty level.

title: Collective seismic reorganization prior to volcanic eruptions: intra-volcano comparisons across Stromboli, Kīlauea, and Icelandic systems
abstract: Live monitoring dashboard: An experimental, non-predictive monitoring interface implementing the same pipeline is available at:https://franjamar-monitor.streamlit.app/ The system runs the identical pipeline in a continuous monitoring configuration (T–3 h delayed window), enabling near-real-time exploration of multistation coherence patterns across multiple seismic and volcanic regions. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- V1.1 This record presents a volcanic-focused extension of the TAMC–FRANJAMAR framework,originally introduced for the retrospective and reproducible analysis ofcollective statistical behavior in multistation seismic networks(see Martinez Sanchez, F. J., TAMC–FRANJAMAR: A retrospective and reproducibleframework for the analysis of collective statistical behavior in multistationseismic networks, Zenodo, DOI: https://zenodo.org/records/18085580 ). While the original implementation was illustrated primarily using large tectonicearthquakes, the present work extends the methodology to volcanic systems,with a particular focus on eruptive episodes at Mount Etna, Kīlauea, and anIcelandic volcanic system.The analysis is designed to investigate how collective seismic organizationemerges and reorganizes in the vicinity of eruptive transitions, using anevent-centered and network-based approach. This repository includes an interactive and configurable analysis pipelinethat automatically retrieves seismic waveform data from public FDSN services(e.g., USGS and IRIS) within user-defined temporal windows.Users can specify eruptive reference times, select matched control periods,and generate null models and placebo tests under a unified methodologicalframework.The pipeline supports systematic comparison across multiple eruptions andacross distinct volcanic systems, enabling inter-volcano analyses underidentical statistical and processing assumptions. Collective seismic reorganization is quantified using network-level metricsthat capture multistation variability, temporal synchrony, and collectivedeviations.All parameters are fixed a priori and applied identically across real events,control windows, and null-model realizations, ensuring methodologicalconservatism and minimizing event-specific tuning or overfitting. In addition to its application to volcano seismology, the TAMC–FRANJAMARframework has been independently extended to other complex dynamical systems,including aerodynamic and turbulent flow analyses(see Martinez Sanchez, F. J., TAMC–FRANJAMAR extension to aerodynamics, Zenodo,DOI: https://zenodo.org/records/18288994), highlighting the generality of the approach beyondgeophysical contexts. This framework is strictly retrospective and methodological.It is not designed, validated, or intended for real-time monitoring,prediction, early warning, or operational decision-making.Any such use falls outside the scope of this work and is not supportedor endorsed by the author. v2 Event-centered multistation TAMC-FRANJAMAR signatures discriminate coupling regimes across extreme events: North Korea (DPRK) family (2013–2017), Beirut (2020), Chelyabinsk (2013), Brumadinho (2019), and 17 supplementary benchmarks https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18532886

title: Bird sound recognition based on photoelectric residual reservoir computing
abstract: To tackle the challenges of low accuracy and high model complexity in noisy bird sound recognition, this work proposes an efficient scheme based on photoelectric residual reservoir computing (RC). The system extracts and preprocesses audio segments, employs an adaptive Mel-frequency cepstral coefficient method for feature extraction, and maps features into a time series via masking. A residual structure with two parallel photoelectric reservoirs is constructed, where the second reservoir learns the residual errors of the first to enhance recognition. Experimental results on 12 bird species show that the residual system achieves 86.5% accuracy, outperforming a single reservoir. Notably, when the first reservoir operates suboptimally (74.1% accuracy), the residual system improves performance by about 10%. This approach maintains low energy consumption and complexity, offering a practical solution for lightweight bioacoustic monitoring.

title: Engineering Analysis and Quantitative Research on the Platform-Based Evolution of Enterprise Communication Systems
abstract: This study, based on long-term engineering practice, conducted a systematic analysis of the evolution process of the enterprise communication system from the application layer to the platform layer. By integrating the operation and maintenance records of multiple communication systems from 2014 to 2024, a quantitative study was carried out from dimensions such as function module reusability, operational complexity, and service capacity. The statistical results show that as the degree of system platformization increases, the reusability of core functional modules has risen from approximately 30% to over 65%. The annual maintenance manpower input has decreased by approximately 35% to 40%. The research results indicate that the platform-based architecture has significant advantages in supporting the long-term evolution and multi-service coordination of enterprise communication systems.

title: Towards a robust adversarial patch attack against RGB-T crowd counting
abstract: Deep learning-based RGB-T crowd counting has attracted increasing attention due to its robustness under diverse environmental conditions, supporting applications in public safety monitoring and smart city systems. However, the vulnerability of such multimodal models to adversarial attacks remains largely unexplored, posing significant threats to their reliability and security in real-world deployments. To address this gap, we propose AttackCounting, a novel adversarial patch attack specifically designed for RGB-T crowd counting models. Unlike existing attack methods that target single-modal inputs, our approach jointly leverages multi-modal saliency from both RGB and thermal domains to identify cross-modal critical regions. By injecting adversarial perturbations into these regions, the attack effectively disrupts the cooperative fusion process between modalities. Furthermore, a local distortion incentive module is introduced to concentrate perturbations in crowd-dense areas while suppressing irrelevant noise. Extensive experiments on several state-of-the-art RGB-T crowd counting models demonstrate that AttackCounting significantly degrades counting accuracy and system reliability. This study exposes fundamental security weaknesses in current RGB-T crowd counting systems and highlights the urgent need for developing attack-resilient multimodal perception models.

title: Transformer-Driven Semi-Supervised Learning for Prostate Cancer Histopathology: A DINOv2–TransUNet Framework
abstract: Prostate cancer is diagnosed through a comprehensive study of histopathology slides, which takes time and requires professional interpretation. To minimize this load, we developed a semi-supervised learning technique that combines transformer-based representation learning and a custom TransUNet classifier. To capture a wide range of morphological structures without manual annotation, our method pretrains DINOv2 on 10,000 unlabeled prostate tissue patches. After receiving the transformer-derived features, a bespoke CNN-based decoder uses residual upsampling and carefully constructed skip connections to merge data from many spatial scales. Expert pathologists identified only 20% of the patches in the whole dataset; the remaining unlabeled samples were contributed by using a consistency-driven learning method that promoted reliable predictions across various augmentations. The model received precision and recall scores of 91.81% and 89.02%, respectively, and an accuracy of 93.78% on an additional test set. These results exceed the performance of a conventional U-Net and a baseline encoder–decoder network. All things considered, the localized CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) decoding and global transformer attention provide a reliable method for prostate cancer classification in situations with little annotated data.

title: A Medical Insurance Question Answering System Based on Multi-Strategy Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: With the growing demand for medical insurance question answering (QA) systems, providing accurate and reliable services amidst complex insurance policies, terminological synonyms, and cross-entity relationships has become a significant challenge. Existing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) methods, while effectively combining information retrieval with generation models, often face issues such as unstable performance across different scenarios and increased generation noise due to their simple fusion methods. To address the aforementioned issues, this paper proposes the Tri-Router, a multi-strategy retrievalaugmented generation framework. It combines three complementary strategies: sparse retrieval (BM25), dense retrieval (DPR), and knowledge graph retrieval (Graph-RAG), and dynamically predicts optimal modal weights via a Transformer attention router to achieve fine-grained retrieval dispatching. Through this mechanism, this paper significantly enhances the retrieval accuracy and generation quality of the QA system in complex scenarios. Experimental results show that the method based on this framework surpasses traditional methods on multiple evaluation metrics, and ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the dynamic routing mechanism and the tri-modal complementary structure.

title: Model-Centric Diagnostics: A Framework for Internal State Readouts
abstract: We present a model-centric diagnostic framework that treats training state as a latent variable and unifies a family of internal readouts -- head-gradient norms, confidence, entropy, margin, and related signals -- as anchor-relative projections of that state. A preliminary version of this work introduced a head-gradient probe for checkpoint selection. In this version, we focus on the unifying perspective and structural diagnostics; full algorithmic details, theoretical analysis, and experimental validation will appear in a forthcoming paper. We outline the conceptual scaffold: any prediction head induces a local loss landscape whose geometry (gradient magnitude, curvature, sharpness) reflects how well the upstream features are aligned with the task. Different readout choices -- gradient norms, softmax entropy, predictive margin -- correspond to different projections of this geometry, each with complementary strengths. The framework suggests that checkpoint selection, early stopping, and lightweight architecture pre-screening can all be viewed as querying the same underlying state through different lenses. Illustrative experiments on ImageNet classification and COCO detection/segmentation hint at the practical potential; rigorous benchmarks and ablations are deferred to the full paper.

title: FASTR: Reimagining FASTQ via Compact Image-inspired Representation
abstract: Abstract Motivation High-throughput sequencing (HTS) enables population-scale genomics but generates massive datasets, creating bottlenecks in storage, transfer, and analysis. FASTQ, the standard format for over two decades, stores one byte per base and one byte per quality score, leading to inefficient I/O, high storage costs, and redundancy. Existing compression tools can mitigate some issues, but often introduce costly decompression or complex dependency issues. Results We introduce FASTR , a lossless, computation-native successor to FASTQ that encodes each nucleotide together with its base quality score into a single 8-bit value. FASTR reduces file size by at least 2× while remaining fully reversible and directly usable for downstream analyses. Applying general-purpose compression tools on FASTR consistently yields higher compression ratios, 2.47, 3.64, and 4.8× faster compression, and 2.34, 1.96, 1.75× faster decompression than on FASTQ across Illumina, HiFi, and ONT reads. FASTR is machine-learning-ready, allowing reads to be consumed directly as numerical vectors or image-like representations. We provide a highly parallel software ecosystem for FASTQ–FASTR conversion and show that FASTR integrates with existing tools, such as minimap2, with minimal interface changes and no performance overhead. By eliminating decompression costs and reducing data movement, FASTR lays the foundation for scalable genomics analyses and real-time sequencing workflows. Availability and Implementation https://github.com/ALSER-Lab/FASTR

title: Neuroadaptive Generative Gaming using Artificial Intelligence and Brain–Computer Interface for Real-Time Storyline Evolution
abstract: The rapid evolution of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) technologies is revolutionizing the way humans interact with digital systems, particularly within the gaming industry.This study introduces and explores the emerging paradigm of Neuroadaptive Generative Gaming, a nextgeneration approach that merges cognitive neuroscience, emotion-aware computing, and generative artificial intelligence to enable dynamically evolving narrative experiences.The core objective of this research is to design a hybridized system in which BCI-derived neural data and Generative AI models collaborate to adapt in-game storylines, missions, dialogues, and environmental factors in real time, in response to a player's cognitive and emotional states.In this proposed framework, the player's brain activity-captured through electroencephalography (EEG) signals-is continuously analyzed using machine learning classifiers to interpret affective states such as engagement, frustration, relaxation, or excitement.These real-time affective indicators are transmitted to a Generative Language Model (LLM) that reconstructs the narrative context dynamically.For instance, when heightened excitement or stress is detected, the system can autonomously alter gameplay intensity, modify environmental tone, or reconfigure dialogue structures to sustain player immersion.Conversely, in calmer states, the system may generate exploratory or story-rich sequences to maintain engagement.The fusion of AI-based generative algorithms with neurophysiological feedback mechanisms leads to the creation of a self-adaptive storytelling ecosystem, where no two gameplay experiences are ever identical.This introduces an unprecedented level of personalization, making the player not just a participant but an integral co-creator of the narrative experience.The neuroadaptive gaming paradigm thus shifts the design philosophy from static, pre-scripted sequences toward emotionally intelligent and cognitively responsive environments that evolve with the user.

title: Fact-Constant / Narrative-Variable Architecture : A Formal Framework for Epistemically Stable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Large language models achieve remarkable performance on language tasks but exhibit systematic failures in factual reliability, reasoning stability, and epistemic transparency. We identify the root cause: modern architectures treat facts and inferences as statistically equivalent tokens, leading to hallucination, fact mutation, and unwarranted confidence. We propose the Fact-Constant / Narrative-Variable (FC/NV) architecture, a hybrid epistemic framework that enforces strict separation between immutable factual constants and mutable explanatory hypotheses. Under FC/NV, reasoning becomes constrained symbolic transformation over verified facts, while language generation remains probabilistic but subordinate to factual integrity. We provide: (1) formal definitions of epistemic categories, (2) architectural specifications, (3) algorithmic implementations, (4) evaluation protocols, (5) theoretical analysis, and (6) empirical validation strategies. The framework is falsifiable, implementable, and compatible with existing neural systems.

title: Innovation and Practice of AI-Empowered Digital Teaching Models for Sports Anatomy
abstract: Addressing the pain points in traditional teaching of Sports Anatomy, this research integrates knowledge graphs with AI technology to establish a new digital teaching model centred on students, driven by data, and combining virtual and physical elements. By constructing macro, meso, and micro-level knowledge graphs, developing a scenario-based teaching resource matrix, innovating a closed-loop teaching process, incorporating ideological and political elements, and building a digital assessment system, the model achieves precise upgrades across the entire teaching process. Empirical comparisons demonstrate that this digital teaching model significantly enhances student engagement, academic performance, and task completion quality. It fosters comprehensive development in innovative literacy and professional identity, while the course development generates positive spillover effects. This approach provides a replicable practical paradigm for the digital transformation of sports-related professional curricula.

title: Research on Time Series Prediction Model of Photovoltaic Power Generation Based on CNN-GRU-Attention
abstract: The power of photovoltaic power generation is significantly affected by the temporal fluctuations of meteorological factors such as temperature and radiation intensity, and its strong intermittency and nonlinearity pose a huge challenge to the real-time dispatching of power systems and the consumption of new energy. Accurate timing prediction is key to ensuring the stable operation of the power grid. In response to the difficulty of traditional prediction methods in capturing local correlations and critical moment features of time series data, and the functional shortcomings of a single deep learning model, combined with seven core influencing factors such as temperature, air pressure, humidity, total radiation, direct radiation, scattered radiation, and historical power generation, A convolutional neural network (CNN) - gated recurrent unit (GRU) -Attention (Attention) fusion prediction model for focused time series modeling (CNN-GRU-Attention) is proposed. The model first eliminates redundant information through feature screening, then uses CNN to extract local correlation features of time series data, captures long time series dependencies of power generation through GRU, and finally introduces the Attention mechanism to assign high weights to the key time series nodes of GRU output to enhance the model 'adaptability to complex conditions. Based on the measured data of a certain photovoltaic power station, the proposed model was compared with traditional statistical methods (ARIMA), machine learning methods (SVM), single deep learning models (GRU, CNN), and fusion models (CNN-GRU). The results show that the MAE, average RMSE, MAPE and R2of the CNN-GRU-Attention model on the test set are 4.8MW, 6.2MW, 2.8% and 0.992, respectively. Compared with the traditional method ARIMA, the various error indicators were reduced by 57.1%, 57.2%, 67.4% respectively, and R2was increased by 0.116; The model is significantly better than the comparison model and provides an efficient solution for ultra-short-term time series prediction of photovoltaic power generation.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Small and Medium Enterprises: Navigating its Promises and Challenges
abstract: The latest technological developments in generative artificial intelligence (GAI) offer powerful capabilities to small and medium enterprises (SMEs), as they facilitate the democratization of both scalability and creativity. Even if they have little technical expertise or financial resources, SMEs can leverage this technology to streamline work processes and unleash innovation, thereby improving their product offerings and long-term competitiveness. This paper discusses how SMEs can navigate both the promises and challenges of GAI and offers a roadmap for deploying GAI. We introduce a sailing metaphor that reveals key strategic dimensions for GAI deployment: competency of employees, effective leadership and work values, organizational culture, collaboration and cooperation, and relationships with third parties. We offer practical recommendations that serve as a useful compass for successfully deploying GAI in SMEs.

title: Boosting Deep Reinforcement Learning with Semantic Knowledge for Robotic Manipulators
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) is a powerful framework for solving complex sequential decision-making problems, particularly in robotic control. However, its practical deployment is often hindered by the substantial amount of experience required for learning, which results in high computational and time costs. In this work, we propose a novel integration of DRL with semantic knowledge in the form of Knowledge Graph Embeddings (KGEs), aiming to enhance learning efficiency by providing contextual information to the agent. Our architecture combines KGEs with visual observations, enabling the agent to exploit environmental knowledge during training. Experimental validation with robotic manipulators in environments featuring both fixed and randomized target attributes demonstrates that our method achieves up to {60}{\%} reduction in learning time and improves task accuracy by approximately 15 percentage points, without increasing training time or computational complexity. These results highlight the potential of semantic knowledge to reduce sample complexity and improve the effectiveness of DRL in robotic applications.

title: Retrieve-Refine-Calibrate: A Framework for Complex Claim Fact-Checking
abstract: Fact-checking aims to verify the truthfulness of a claim based on the retrieved evidence. Existing methods typically follow a decomposition paradigm, in which a claim is broken down into sub-claims that are individually verified. However, the decomposition paradigm may introduce noise to the verification process due to irrelevant entities or evidence, ultimately degrading verification accuracy. To address this problem, we propose a Retrieve-Refine-Calibrate (RRC) framework based on large language models (LLMs). Specifically, the framework first identifies the entities mentioned in the claim and retrieves evidence relevant to them. Then, it refines the retrieved evidence based on the claim to reduce irrelevant information. Finally, it calibrates the verification process by re-evaluating low-confidence predictions. evidence.title: Retrieve-Refine-Calibrate: A Framework for Complex Claim Fact-Checking
evidence.abstract: Fact-checking aims to verify the truthfulness of a claim based on the retrieved evidence. Existing methods typically follow a decomposition paradigm, in which a claim is broken down into sub-claims that are individually verified. However, the decomposition paradigm may introduce noise to the verification process due to irrelevant entities or evidence, ultimately degrading verification accuracy. title: Persistence Limits Under Vanishing Noise in Fault-Tolerant Quantum Systems Irreducible Maintenance Costs Independent of Physical Error Rates
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation is often analyzed in the limit of vanishing physical noise, where logical error rates per operation can be made arbitrarily small. This limit is sometimes interpreted as implying that the physical cost of maintaining quantum information may likewise vanish. In this work, we show that this inference is incorrect for systems that preserve logical identity through sustained error correction. Even as physical noise approaches zero, the irreversible classical maintenance required to extract, process, and reset syndrome information imposes a non-vanishing thermodynamic cost. As a result, persistence limits on sustained quantum identity do not disappear in the ideal-noise limit. The constraint arises from irreversible identity maintenance rather than from noise suppression or imperfect hardware. This work is intentionally descriptive and non-operational, identifying a structural persistence bound without proposing mechanisms, architectures, or control strategies.

title: A Formal Protocol for Disciplinary Transition: From Φ-Operators to Mathematical Systems
abstract: This paper presents a formal protocol for transitioning from discourse based on non-formal conceptual operators (Φ-operators) to rigorous mathematical reasoning. We define the class Φ of operators characterized by the absence of a complete formal system axiomatizing their derivability predicate. The central theorem demonstrates that for any Φ-operator O, the set O(K)∖K generated from a consistent knowledge base K contains only (1) statements lacking determinate truth value, (2) logical tautologies, or (3) empirical hypotheses. We provide constructive isomorphisms mapping five canonical Φ-operators (labeled O_H, O_D, O_G, O_De, O_W) to formal systems, showing these mappings are either exact or involve bounded approximation errors. The protocol's soundness is established via complexity bounds derived from the Universal Parameterization Framework (UPF). A verifiable algorithmic criterion completes the transition. This work provides formal justification for focusing exclusively on mathematical systems for generating non-trivial necessary knowledge, while itself operating as a meta-mathematical analysis rather than philosophical discourse.

title: Generation of Chinese Arithmetic Word Problems with Controllable Difficulty Levels Based on Pre-trained Models
abstract: Problem generation, as a natural language generation task, has garnered significant attention from researchers in recent years. Among these, the generation of controllably difficult Chinese arithmetic word problems stands as a core task underpinning personalized mathematics education. However, existing methods still face three challenges: (1) limited annotated datasets with missing labels and small scales, and costly, subjective manual annotation; (2) narrow difficulty feature dimensions, with existing work only selecting structured features and failing to extract unstructured ones automatically; (3) severe generation bias, where mainstream models produce results with large difficulty deviations from expectations, unable to meet refined teaching needs. To resolve these, this paper proposes the CLT-MathGCO framework based on CLT-MATH theory: it auto-expands datasets via entity substitution and numerical perturbation, and realizes fine-grained six-dimensional difficulty control and precise generation through soft-prompt difficulty injection and an enhanced difficulty calibrator. Experiments show the framework achieves a six-dimensional difficulty hit rate of 0.837, average single-dimensional accuracy of 0.935, 0.958 validity rate and 28.9 BLEU-4 score for generated problems, offering an effective technical approach for efficient personalized educational resource generation.

title: Causal Self-Supervised Graph Learning for Robust PV Power Forecasting Against Distribution Shift
abstract: Due to stochastic weather changes and the increasing frequency of extreme weather events in recent years, photovoltaic (PV) power generation data frequently undergo probability distribution shifts in practice. This poses huge challenges for traditional machine learning-based power forecasting methods that rely on unstable correlations between input and output for predictions. To this end, this paper proposes a causal self-supervised graph learning framework for robust power forecasting of multiple PV sites. Specifically, a structural causal model is first built to describe the PV power generation process, which allows us to distinguish the confounder that causes the failure of prior studies. Then, the spurious correlations caused by the confounder are removed through causality intervention with do-calculus and back-door adjustment, which is further solved by our proposed theoretical solution, termed PV generation environment disentangled adaptation (PV-EDA). After that, a self-supervised multi-view graph neural network is devised to implement PV-EDA in a fidelity way, such that causality intervention is effectively realized within the designed forecasting model. The stable causality improves the generalization ability of the proposed model and allows it to achieve robust forecasting performance under varying distributional shift scenarios. Numerical experiments are conducted on real-world PV power output data to evaluate the model's day-ahead forecasting performance. The results show that the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art PV forecasting approaches under various distribution shift scenarios.

title: Few-Shot Transfer Learning for Cross-Subject Visual Brain Decoding via Whole-Brain Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging
abstract: A critical challenge in fMRI-based visual brain decoding is that models trained on data from individual subjects cannot generalize to new participants without extensive retraining. To address this issue, this study proposes a multi-subject transfer learning approach based on whole-brain fMRI data, which not only achieves competitive within-subject decoding performance, but also enables cross-subject generalization via fine-tuning with a small amount of data. In this study, ResNet model is trained on brain imaging data from 6 NSD subjects, achieving a Top-1 retrieval accuracy of 85.8% on the subjects included in the training set. For completely unseen new subjects without any fine-tuning, the model still reaches an accuracy of 2.3%, which is significantly superior to previous whole-brain multi-subject decoding methods (1.0%). More importantly, after fine-tuning with only 5% of the new subject-specific data, the model’s Top-5 retrieval accuracy is improved to 71.5%. In summary, this study confirms that brain decoding models can achieve cross-individual generalization by learning shared neural representations across subjects, which drastically reduces the task’s data requirement per subject and lays a foundation for the practical application of related technologies.

title: Multitask Learning and BERT Embedding: A Comprehensive Approach to Subjectivity Detection and Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
abstract: The proliferation of online platforms has intensified the need for fine-grained sentiment analysis of customer reviews. While traditional Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) focuses on sentiment classification, it often overlooks the crucial distinction between subjective opinions and objective statements. This paper introduces the Subjectivity Multitask Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis framework, which integrates Subjectivity Detection as an auxiliary task with Aspect Sentiment Classification through a unified multitask learning architecture. The model leverages BERT embeddings, a Bidirectional LSTM, a self-attention mechanism, and a Neural Tensor Network to effectively model the interplay between subjectivity and sentiment. Crucially, our experimental results on the comprehensive MEMD multi-domain dataset demonstrate the framework’s effectiveness, achieving a state-of-the-art F1-score of 87.26%. This represents a significant 26.89 percentage point improvement over the previous baseline, showcasing superior performance in both precision-recall balance and cross-domain stability. Key contributions include: (1) manual annotation of aspect-level subjectivity labels for a large-scale multi-domain dataset, (2) development of an integrated multitask framework that addresses precision-recall imbalance in ABSA, and (3) empirical validation showing consistent improvements across diverse domains. Results confirm that joint optimization of related tasks enhances sentiment classification accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency.

title: Hybrid Poly Commitments for Scalable Binius Zero-Knowledge Proofs in Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training without sharing raw data, but practical deployments increasingly require verifiable guarantees that clients compute updates correctly. Zero-knowledge proofs can provide such guarantees, yet existing approaches face scalability limits due to the combined cost of polynomial commitments and fast Fourier transform (FFT) intensive verification. Pairing-based schemes offer compact proofs but incur high prover and verifier overhead, while hash-based constructions reduce algebraic cost at the expense of rapidly growing proof sizes. This paper proposes Hybrid-Commit, a polynomial commitment architecture for Binius zero-knowledge proofs that aligns cryptographic primitives with the algebraic structure of federated learning workloads. The scheme separates verification into additive and multiplicative phases: linear aggregation is handled using batched additive commitments optimized for binary fields, while non-linear constraints are verified via hash-based commitments over sparsely selected FFT domains. Proofs from multiple clients are combined through recursive aggregation while preserving non-interactivity. Experiments demonstrate scalability in prover time and proof size (near-constant prover time across 4–11 clients; 160 bytes per client representing 341× and 813× reductions vs. FRI-PCS and Orion), although verification time (762 ms per client) does not scale favorably, making the scheme suitable for bandwidth-constrained scenarios. The scheme achieves under 2% end-to-end training overhead with no impact on model accuracy, indicating that workload-aware commitment design can improve specific scalability dimensions of zero-knowledge verification in federated learning systems.

title: Requirements and Application Design for a Digital-intelligent Warfare Case Teaching System
abstract: Warfare case based teaching, as a vital component of case-based pedagogy, plays a significant role in mass education. However, it faces challenges such as fragmented resource materials, limited teaching methodologies, and suboptimal instructional quality and effectiveness. Developing a digital and intelligent warfare case based teaching system that integrates digital and intelligent technologies can effectively address the current issues confronting warfare case based teaching. This paper analyses typical problems in traditional warfare case based teaching, distils requirements for constructing a digital-intelligent warfare case based teaching system, outlines its overall architectural design, and explores application concepts. It provides effective guidance for advancing innovative reforms in digital-intelligent warfare case based teaching.

title: HIN-OOD: An Out-of-Distribution Analysis System for Heterogeneous Graphs
abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization remains a key challenge in heterogeneous graph learning, where graph neural networks often degrade under structural or semantic shifts. We present HIN-OOD, an interactive visual analytics system for diagnosing OOD behaviors in heterogeneous graph neural networks. The system integrates statistical analysis and visualization to reveal how degree, homophily, and feature biases influence model robustness. A meta-path-centric design quantifies semantic divergence and ablation effects, while coordinated bar charts and tabular views link "where distributions shift" to "how performance changes." Through experiments on ACM, IMDB, and DBLP, HIN-OOD enables researchers to visually explore structural and semantic instability, identify fragile or redundant relations, and gain interpretable insights into OOD generalization in graph learning.

title: Too guilty to be unethical: the impact of service robots’ empathy ability on unethical consumer behavior
abstract: Integrating empathy ability into service robots can be regarded as a potential resolution to enhance harmonious human-robot interaction experiences. However, it remains unclear whether and how service robots’ empathy ability impacts unethical consumer behavior (UCB). Therefore, according to social exchange theory, this research explores how service robots’ empathy ability impacts UCB and the underlying mechanism. Through four experiments, we discover that service robots’ empathy ability reduces UCB, with anticipatory guilt serving as the mediator. Moreover, the salience of anticipatory guilt weakens the impact of empathy ability on UCB. Additionally, consumers’ social desirability moderates the impact of service robots’ empathy ability on UCB through anticipatory guilt. title: Frame-Guided Synthetic Claim Generation for Automatic Fact-Checking Using High-Volume Tabular Data
abstract: Automated fact-checking benchmarks have largely ignored the challenge of verifying claims against real-world, high-volume structured data, instead focusing on small, curated tables. We introduce a new large-scale, multilingual dataset to address this critical gap. It contains 78,503 synthetic claims grounded in 434 complex OECD tables, which average over 500K rows each. We propose a novel, frame-guided methodology where algorithms programmatically select significant data points based on six semantic frames to generate realistic claims in English, Chinese, Spanish, and Hindi. Crucially, we demonstrate through knowledge-probing experiments that LLMs have not memorized these facts, forcing systems to perform genuine retrieval and reasoning rather than relying on parameterized knowledge. We provide a baseline SQL-generation system and show that our benchmark is highly challenging. Our analysis identifies evidence retrieval as the primary bottleneck, with models struggling to find the correct data in massive tables. This dataset provides a critical new resource for advancing research on this unsolved, real-world problem.

title: Orbitopal Fixing in SAT
abstract: Despite their sophisticated heuristics, boolean satisfiability (SAT) solvers are still vulnerable to symmetry, causing them to visit search regions that are symmetric to ones already explored. While symmetry handling is routine in other solving paradigms, integrating it into state-of-the-art proof-producing SAT solvers is difficult: added reasoning must be fast, non-interfering with solver heuristics, and compatible with formal proof logging. To address these issues, we present a practical static symmetry breaking approach based on orbitopal fixing, a technique adapted from mixed-integer programming. Our approach adds only unit clauses, which minimizes downstream slowdowns, and it emits succinct proof certificates in the substitution redundancy proof system. Implemented in the satsuma tool, our methods deliver consistent speedups on symmetry-rich benchmarks with negligible regressions elsewhere.

title: Understanding and Improving UMAP with Geometric and Topological Priors: The JORC-UMAP Algorithm
abstract: Nonlinear dimensionality reduction techniques, particularly UMAP, are widely used for visualizing high-dimensional data. However, UMAP's local Euclidean distance assumption often fails to capture intrinsic manifold geometry, leading to topological tearing and structural collapse. We identify UMAP's sensitivity to the k-nearest neighbor graph as a key cause. To address this, we introduce Ollivier-Ricci curvature as a geometric prior, reinforcing edges at geometric bottlenecks and reducing redundant links. Since curvature estimation is noise-sensitive, we also incorporate a topological prior using Jaccard similarity to ensure neighborhood consistency. The resulting method, JORC-UMAP, better distinguishes true manifold structure from spurious connections. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show that JORC-UMAP reduces tearing and collapse more effectively than standard UMAP and other DR methods, as measured by SVM accuracy and triplet preservation scores, while maintaining computational efficiency. This work offers a geometry-aware enhancement to UMAP for more faithful data visualization.

title: Detecting Cardiac Amyloidosis in Italian Cardiology Reports: Structured Variable Extraction versus Direct Free-Text Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Early and accurate identification of cardiac amyloidosis improves patient outcomes, yet relevant evidence is frequently hidden in free-text records. This study assesses whether structured variable extraction or direct free-text analysis more reliably identifies patients with cardiac amyloidosis, with the goal of informing clinical decision support strategies. Methods We extracted 21 clinical variables from 432 Italian patient records using supervised and prompt-based methods with both proprietary and locally-deployable computational models. Classification performance was evaluated by comparing extracted data with gold-standard manual annotations. Two feature sets were tested: general clinical variables and amyloidosis-specific risk factors. Additionally, we evaluated direct zero-shot prediction on unstructured clinical notes. Results For entity extraction, GPT-4.1-mini achieved F1=0.96, comparable to supervised SpaCy (F1=0.95) and GPT-4o (F1=0.94). Local open-source models like Qwen2.5 reached F1=0.94. For cardiac amyloidosis classification, machine learning models using full extracted features matched gold-standard results (SauerkrautLM-Gemma: F1=0.80 vs. gold: F1=0.82). General clinical features alone yielded lower performance (F1=0.68), highlighting that amyloidosis-specific risk factors in unstructured text provide discriminative diagnostic value. Zero-shot direct predictions outperformed supervised feature-based approaches (MedGemma: F1=0.92). Conclusions Automated extraction and zero-shot prediction effectively structure Italian EHRs and identify amyloidosis patients without manual annotation. Domain-specific risk factors in free-text notes provide substantial predictive value. Italian hospitals can potentially deploy locally-deployable models to screen cardiac amyloidosis without manual annotation or proprietary APIs, enabling privacy-preserving clinical decision support in real-world settings.

title: "IHP Open Dataset for Power and Electromagnetic Side-Channel Analysis of B-233 ECC Hardware Implementations"
abstract: "This dataset provides synchronized power consumption and electromagnetic emanation measurements of five hardware implementations of Montgomery scalar multiplication for elliptic curve cryptography over the B-233 binary field, realized on FPGA and ASIC platforms and measured under controlled, repeatable conditions. It contains traces for 31 combinations of input points and secret scalars. The dataset is designed to support a broad range of side-channel analysis scenarios, including non-profiled and profiling attacks, making it a reusable benchmark for evaluating leakage and developing new SCA techniques."

title: Design and Implementation of an AI-Driven Intelligent English Tutoring System for Personalized Language Learning
abstract: Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS) increasingly employ artificial intelligence to support adaptive language learning, yet many systems provide limited integration between learner modeling, activity selection, and feedback delivery. This study presents an English tutoring system that incorporates Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to support personalized instruction through conversational interaction, automated speech recognition, and feedback generation. The system architecture and learning workflow are described, with an emphasis on how learner interaction data are used to u ate learner models and guide adaptive content selection. A pilot study and a controlled experimental evaluation are conducted to examine the feasibility of the approach. Learners using the system show higher post-test gains and greater engagement than those following non-adaptive self-study methods. The contribution of NLP-based feedback mechanisms, including grammatical error correction and dialogue-based practice, is further analyzed, and system performance is examined using quantitative metrics such as the F1 score for error detection and BLEU for feedback generation. Practical issues related to feedback reliability, learner motivation, and alignment with pedagogical practices are also discussed.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Chinese Weibo Based on BERT-BiLSTM-CNN
abstract: With the rapid development of social media, Weibo has become an important platform for expressing public emotions and opinions. Sentiment analysis, as a key task in natural language processing, is of great significance for understanding users’ sentiment orientations and monitoring public opinions. In order to more effectively capture the semantic and emotional information in Weibo texts, a Chinese Weibo sentiment analysis model based on BERT-BiLSTM-CNN is proposed. This model utilizes the BERT pre-trained language model to obtain the contextual semantic representation of the text, captures the sequential features of the text through BiLSTM, and combines CNN to extract local features, ultimately achieving sentiment classification. The experimental results show that this model achieves good performance in the task of Chinese Weibo sentiment analysis, with higher accuracy and F1 scores compared to other deep learning models.
